Cinematic 16:9 golden-hour coastal commercial still, modern social-first lifestyle photography with tactile editorial energy and clean true-to-life color. SCARLETT (Image 1) in a black long-sleeve rash vest still faintly damp against the skin under a crumpled oversized white shirt yanked on over it and simple flip-flops, lived-in coral mouth unblotted, caught mid-stride along the metal safety rail as she lifts a dripping mango ice toward her mouth in the charged instant before a real bite from the side, sticky orange juice already running in rivulets down the ice, free hand hovering near the rail, unfussy no-vanity posture of someone who belongs here. Wide pale-concrete Bondi promenade running above the sand, sun-bleached walkway stretching past a rack of rental surfboards and low beach infrastructure, simple metal rail catching late gold, ocean opening beyond in late-afternoon blue-green with a set rolling through, distant joggers softened into bokeh, open sky going warm. Warm late high-key golden sunlight, a little gold on skin-adjacent rail and the mango ice, bright natural directional late-day light with clean shadows, crisp whites, slight warmth in the highlights, lifted airy shadows, mango orange popping against pale concrete and ocean. Handheld eye-level three-quarter lifestyle frame with natural micro-energy, shallow depth of field holding her and the dripping ice sharp while the promenade and water fall softly behind.
